study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Pregnancies ending in early fetal death or stillbirth
non-immune hydrops fetalis (NIHF) with negative standard-of-care evaluations
cohort: 40 pregnancies complicated by NIHF with negative work-ups for common causes
finding: Pregnancies complicated by NIHF with negative standard-of-care evaluations were associated with several adverse maternal outcomes, including pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, postpartum hemorrhage, and worsened mental health.
mod_finding: Of the 15 live births, 8 (53.3%) were delivered by primary cesarean delivery; 5 (62.5%) were for hydrops fetalis.
